title: U.S. Restores Some Vaccine and Health Aid to Unicef, Gavi and World Food Programme
partialText: The amount is still far below what the U.S. spent previously on humanitarian and health aid, but resumes the flow of money for key efforts to fight malnutrition and disease.

title: Trump’s Polling Numbers Hit a New Low. Don’t Expect Him to Change Course.
partialText: Barely a third of Americans approve of Mr. Trump’s handling of the job, putting him at historic depths for a second-term president at this stage of his tenure.

title: In Dropping Reflecting Pool Case, Pirro Draws Trump’s Wrath
partialText: Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney in Washington, blamed shoddy construction, contradicting President Trump’s pet theory. Mr. Trump said he disagreed “100%” with her.

title: How a Top Law Firm Went From Standing Up to Trump to Bending the Knee
partialText: Paul Weiss was a progressive stalwart for decades and led the legal resistance against President Trump in his first term. Then it surrendered without a fight. This is the inside story of its transformation.

title: Trump, Paul Weiss and the Capitulation of Big Law: 5 Takeaways
partialText: The law firm Paul Weiss led the legal resistance against President Trump. Then it led a sudden retreat across the legal industry. A Times investigation examined how it caved to White House pressure.

title: Iran Plotted Wider War With Help of Its Proxies
partialText: During a fleeting truce, Iranians covertly devised a plan to raise the war’s costs for President Trump if U.S. forces attacked anew.

title: Can Democratic Socialists Agree on Anything? They Say That’s Not the Point.
partialText: At a national summit of the Democratic Socialists of America, nervous energy and a sprawling tableau of sometimes-competing interests were on display.

title: Five Big Moments in Michigan’s Democratic Senate Primary
partialText: Divisions over Israel and high-profile endorsements have shaped the closely-watched race between a progressive former public health official and a more moderate member of Congress.

title: Chicago’s Mayoral Race Is Taking Shape. But What About the Incumbent?
partialText: Several prominent Democrats already are running for mayor of Chicago. Mayor Brandon Johnson has not said whether he will seek a second term next year.

title: How China Keeps Tabs on Foreigners
partialText: An unsecured police dashboard was a rare window into how the authorities track foreigners by collecting and aggregating vast amounts of private data.

title: The Allure and Peril of Riding an Alaskan Wave for Six Miles
partialText: The tidal bore that rockets up the Turnagain Arm south of Anchorage can carry a surfer for an hour; it can also kill. Now that the secret is out, how long will authorities allow surfers to catch the wave?

title: Christopher Nolan’s Trojan Horse

title: Keep on Truckin’

title: La Guaira Is Unrecognizable After Venezuela’s Deadly Earthquakes
